title: Onshape FeatureScript Modeling Safety
summary: Official FeatureScript modeling guidance emphasizes solved sketches before downstream operations, query-based robustness, and explicit geometric references such as Line axes for revolves.
modeling_notes: Use newSketchOnPlane and call skSolve before any opExtrude, opRevolve, opLoft, or opSweep.
Prefer stable queries over direct geometry assumptions.
Revolve axes should be explicit Line values, not edge queries.
feature_pattern: sketch -> skSolve -> downstream solid operation with stable queries.
example_prompt: Create a parametric custom feature with robust query handling

title: Onshape FeatureScript Fillet And Chamfer Query Safety
summary: FeatureScript finishing operations are safest when they target stable edge subsets rather than all edges of a body; shell, fillet, and chamfer should be applied only after the supporting solid exists.
modeling_notes: Never apply whole-body blind edge queries for finishing on generated parts.
Use face- or step-scoped queries wherever possible.
Keep fillet radii below local edge span to reduce regeneration failures.
feature_pattern: solid body -> stable edge selection -> finishing operation.
example_prompt: Create a train cab with safe finishing operations

title: FRCDesign Capture Design Intent For Belt And Chain
summary: FRC-oriented FeatureScripts emphasize capturing design intent from drivetrains and belt or chain runs through editable center distances, component spacing, and modular mechanical interfaces instead of hardcoded geometry.
modeling_notes: Treat belt and chain spacing as computed design parameters.
Do not invent interface locations silently for drivetrain assemblies.
Use retrieved spacing rules to size supporting plates and mounting interfaces.
feature_pattern: design intent parameters -> spacing variables -> support geometry.
validation_rules: support geometry references retrieved spacing intent
example_prompt: Create a belt-driven side plate using standard pulley spacing rules

title: FRCDesign Structural Tube And Mounting Patterns
summary: FRC community FeatureScripts often model structural tube, bearing interfaces, and robot mounts as explicit, editable profiles with consistent hole and bore patterns rather than ad hoc primitives.
modeling_notes: Use parametric tube and plate profiles for structural members.
Keep bore and mounting pattern dimensions exposed in precondition.
Treat bearing and shaft interfaces as primary design features, not afterthought cuts.
feature_pattern: structural profile -> interface bores and holes -> finishing only if stable.
validation_rules: mounting holes and bores remain editable
example_prompt: Create a 2x1 FRC tube with bearing and mounting pattern

title: Alex Kempen Robotics FeatureScript Practices
summary: Robotics-oriented FeatureScript utilities for shafts, bores, and reusable robot parts reinforce explicit interface parameters, reusable profiles, and assembly-minded geometry organization.
modeling_notes: Keep rotary interfaces parameterized and assembly-aware.
Prefer reusable interface geometry over generic cylinders.
Complex mechanisms should expose their key interfaces even when overall dimensions are inferred.
feature_pattern: interface parameters -> reusable shaft/bore geometry -> structural support bodies.
validation_rules: complex prompts do not collapse to primitive placeholders
example_prompt: Create a swerve module with shaft and bearing interfaces
